summary: Every skill row may affect qualification and every qualifying candidate must be returned in sorted order, matching one filtered aggregation followed by output ordering.

optimality.symbol: n input rows and c output candidates
optimality.argument: Any row can supply a candidate's final missing skill, requiring inspection of all n rows, while arbitrary qualifying IDs must be returned in ascending order; the query scans once, groups filtered rows, and sorts only the c winners.

replacement_checks.evidence: An unseen input row can change a candidate from incomplete to complete, and arbitrary winner IDs require ordered output.
Membership filtering and hash aggregation are linear in the input, followed by sorting c qualifying IDs.
Cases cover missing, exact, and extra skills, empty output, numeric ordering, and skills split across candidates.
